notification_verification_v3_15_10._comment: v3.15.10 Phase 3. Findings record only; NOT consumed by any guard. Establishes, per platform, whether the two end-of-task notification triggers can be expressed at all. Trigger A = 'the agent is blocked on the human' (permission request or idle waiting for input). Trigger B = 'the agent finished responding'. A trigger is delivered ONLY when its event name is verified against first-party documentation: an unverified name ships a hook that is registered, executable, and permanently inert, which escalation-trigger.sh already did for four minor versions.

claude.note: Delivered in Phase 1. Notification fires on permission requests and on idle-waiting-for-input.

cursor.note: Fetched first-party 2026-08-04. The documented set is 21 events across agent, Tab, and app-lifecycle groups. `stop` is documented as 'Handle agent completion' and carries trigger B. NOTHING in the set means 'blocked on the human': `beforeShellExecution` can return an 'ask' permission status but fires before EVERY shell command, so a notifier there would recreate the per-turn storm this release removed. Trigger A is therefore omitted rather than approximated. `subagentStop` exists in Cursor and is deliberately not wired.

qwen.source: v3.15.8 Phase 6 first-party verification of the Qwen Code hooks documentation
qwen.note: Qwen KEPT the Claude-style event names and the verified list is explicit and closed: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop, PreCompact. No Notification equivalent, so trigger A is unavailable. Trigger B is expressible via Stop but NOT delivered in v3.15.10: deferred rather than rushed, because Qwen's hooks merge into its own settings.json and that writer needs its own test surface. Tracked as a v3.15.11 candidate.

gemini-cli.source: v3.15.8 Phase 6 first-party verification of the upstream hooks reference
gemini-cli.note: Gemini CLI RENAMED every lifecycle event relative to the Claude-style set: PreToolUse -> BeforeTool, Stop -> AfterAgent, PreCompact -> PreCompress. So trigger B is `AfterAgent`, and writing `Stop` here would be exactly the inert-hook defect this phase exists to prevent. No notification-equivalent event is documented. NOT delivered: Gemini CLI is enterprise-only opt-in post-2026-06-18 (--enterprise flag), so it is the lowest-value target of the set.

codex.source: openai/codex implementation: codex-rs/hooks/src/events/permission_request.rs + serde wire names in codex-rs/hooks/src/lib.rs
codex.note: SETTLED 2026-08-04 (v3.15.11), upgrading the v3.15.10 UNVERIFIED verdict. openai/codex ships no docs/hooks.md, so the event set was verified against the IMPLEMENTATION instead of prose: codex-rs/hooks/src/events/ contains a dedicated permission_request.rs module, and the serde wire names in codex-rs/hooks/src/lib.rs enumerate the full set as PermissionRequest, PostCompact, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PreToolUse, SessionEnd, SessionStart, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit. PermissionRequest is Codex's 'blocked on the human' event, which makes Codex the ONLY platform besides Claude Code able to express trigger A. Both triggers are now delivered: Nexus-Hub's Notification chain is aliased onto PermissionRequest via CODEX_EVENT_ALIASES, and Stop carries the completion hook. Two v3.15.10 defects were found and fixed while settling this. (1) The Notification chain was being dropped as 'no Codex event of that name' because no alias existed. (2) notify-on-complete WAS reaching Codex but _notify_common.sh was NOT: the module is deliberately unregistered in settings.json, so the settings-driven script collection never saw it, and the hook sourced nothing and exited silently on every run. Both were the same shape as the inert-hook failure this verification discipline exists to prevent, and both are now asserted by test.

kimi.note: The v3.15.8 verification established Kimi's hook SCHEMA (a [[hooks]] array in ~/.kimi-code/config.toml permitting ONLY event/matcher/command/timeout, where extra fields make the config fail to load) and its tool-matcher mapping, but did NOT enumerate the event names. Global scope only. Nothing delivered until the event set is verified.

copilot.note: PERMANENT NON-COVERAGE for notifications. Copilot exposes no hook surface of its own; it receives instruction text plus an opt-in skills wrapper set. It IS fully covered by the v3.15.10 end-of-task summary rule, which needs only an instruction surface. Do not re-litigate.

opencode.note: PERMANENT NON-COVERAGE for notifications. OpenCode's plugins/ is a JS/TS Bun module runtime exporting an event API; a .sh or .py hook cannot be dropped in and run (documented non-gap DF-4, hooks_supported stays False). Delivering these triggers would mean authoring and maintaining a Bun plugin, which is out of scope. OpenCode IS fully covered by the end-of-task summary rule. Do not re-litigate.

notification_verification_v3_15_10.summary: Trigger A is expressible on exactly TWO verified platforms (Claude Code via Notification, Codex via PermissionRequest). Trigger B is verified on four (Claude Code, Cursor, Qwen, and Codex) and renamed-but-verified on a fifth (Gemini CLI's AfterAgent). As of v3.15.11 both triggers are delivered to Claude Code and Codex, and trigger B to Cursor. Qwen and Gemini CLI remain expressible-but-undelivered; Kimi's event set is still unenumerated. Copilot and OpenCode are permanently out of reach for notifications and are fully covered by the end-of-task summary rule.
notification_verification_v3_15_10.df1_settlement: DF-1 SETTLED 2026-08-04 against first-party Cursor documentation, and the v3.15.9 finding is OVERTURNED. cursor.com/docs/skills documents FOUR skills read-paths, two of them user-level: '.agents/skills/', '.cursor/skills/', '~/.agents/skills/' (global), and '~/.cursor/skills/' (global), plus backward-compatible '.claude/skills/' and '.codex/skills/'. Discovery walks the root RECURSIVELY. So the global ~/.cursor/skills write is CORRECT and load-bearing, and the v3.15.9 release note that extended DF-1 to that path on secondary evidence was wrong; that extension is withdrawn. The COMMANDS half is different: Cursor's own docs no longer document a commands directory at all, Cursor 2.4 ships a /migrate-to-skills skill that converts both user-level and workspace-level commands into skills with disable-model-invocation:true, and a community bug report titled 'Commands are not detected in the global cursor directory' reports the global path does not work. Nexus-Hub already delivers every command as a command-skill through the verified skills path, so the global ~/.cursor/commands write is REDUNDANT rather than load-bearing. It is RETAINED unchanged for now (writing a directory Cursor ignores is harmless; removing one it does read would silently drop coverage), and flagged for deliberate removal in a later release.
